To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
U1A, the protein that binds to and stabilizes U1 snRNA, binds to the survival motor neuron 3′-untranslated region (3′-UTRs) and inhibits poly(A) site selection and cleavage and poly(A) site usage.
the U1A snRNP protein binds to and regulates polyadenylation of SMN mRNA.
the U1A snRNP protein inhibits 3′ end cleavage and poly(A) addition to the SMN mRNA and thereby regulates the expression of the survival protein, which is deficient in spinal muscular atrophy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the expression of the SMN gene is regulated.
the molecular mechanisms of RNA processing and their impact on gene expression.
understanding the molecular basis of spinal muscular atrophy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
U1A is a key regulator of the 3’ processing of the SMNN mRNA and that it does this by directly binding to the SMNN 3’-UTR and inhibiting 3’ cleavage by the CstF complex.
U1A is a key regulator of the SMN gene and is critical to the expression of SMN protein, and thus is a critical regulator to the survival of motor neurons.
U1A protein regulates 3′ processing (polyadenylation) of the survival motorneuron (SMN) mRNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
U1A is a critical regulator for SMN expression.
U1A regulates 3′ processing and therefore expression of the SMN mRNA.
U1A is a key regulator of survival motor neuron expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified U1A as a critical regulator of survival motor neuron mRNA processing and expression.
U1A is a critical regulator for the expression of SMN.
the U1A component of the U snRNP is a critical regulator for expression of the SMN mRNA and that U1A is a key player in the regulation of SMNs expression.
